audit-template-format.title: Stage 2 audit-control-issue template requires a spec-tailored verification checklist and a structured report format (severity table, per-finding evidence, verification-performed checklist, explicit verdict)
audit-template-format.note: From issue #14 item 1: the audit template is unstandardized and Codex's responses can come back too short to trust. Model it on Covenant issue #88 (https://github.com/LouPineWays/Covenant/issues/88), whose audit-control-issue body carried a numbered, change-specific verification checklist and required-output spec, and whose Codex response (https://github.com/LouPineWays/Covenant/issues/88#issuecomment-5351402128) returned a severity table, per-finding evidence, and a verification-performed checklist. This repo's own .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/audit-control-issue.yml scope/findings fields are currently generic prose prompts, not that structure.

subagent-chat-discipline.title: AGENTS.md requires implementation work between issues/PRs to be delegated to subagents by default, so top-level chat stays to the fixed kickoff/decision/question/completion/blocked lines
subagent-chat-discipline.note: From issue #14 item 2: founder is still seeing step-by-step process chatter in Claude Code chat. AGENTS.md already has a Subagent dispatch section and fixed chat report formats, but frames delegation as merely 'approved,' not default/required for implementation work itself. Tighten the language so internal implementation steps are subagent-dispatched by default and top-level chat is limited to the fixed one-line formats already defined in AGENTS.md. Tracked in issue #16, PR #17.

done.evidence: AGENTS.md Subagent dispatch section tightened; see PR #17

audit-issue-reuse-guard.title: Bounded-review-cycle guards against reusing a non-audit issue for the Stage 2 @codex trigger, or declaring a verdict without an actual audit response
audit-issue-reuse-guard.note: From issue #14 item 3: on issue #9 (the original feature issue, already closed by PR #10's merge), @codex review was posted directly on it instead of opening a fresh audit-control-issue; Codex replied BLOCKED (no PR-creation tool available in that write-shaped context) and Claude Code then self-declared CLEAN without a real Codex audit response. Issue #11 was then opened properly per docs/bounded-review-cycle.md and found 2 real P2 bugs the sham CLEAN missed. bounded-review-cycle.md already documents the correct Stage 2 procedure (fresh audit-control-issue, never invoke @codex from two places) but has no explicit rule against reusing a non-audit issue as the Stage 2 control boundary, nor against recording a verdict with no actual audit response comment behind it. Add both as explicit guards.
